targets.title: Or35a coding sequence for assembly into an olfactory receptor expression system
targets.body_markdown:
### Intended role and assembly

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This CDS supplies the Or35a subunit. For this platform it is co-expressed with the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`; a response depends on the assembled system and the cellular context. The isolated sequence is not a complete sensing device.

Use this part to choose your own promoter, expression marker or fusion arrangement. The corresponding bicistronic module includes a GCCACC initiation context and IRES-mCherry. For either design, supply suitable transcriptional control and polyadenylation from the mammalian vector, and verify start/stop codons and reading frame against the actual assembled sequence. Expression, localization and channel function require separate checks.

### Functional architecture

![Or35a CDS in the expression-module context](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/8d74a99ca32a4b1638861e91f2aa49ca1befbe810331c315cd27a9a385e1e145.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted Or35a CDS is the basic part; GCCACC initiation context, EMCV IRES and mCherry belong to the assembled expression module, not this isolated sequence. The calcium-reporter/Orco construct is a separate partner. The diagram does not assert experimental localization or activity.*

### Sequence provenance

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0028946](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0028946.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0080781 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_723916](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_723916) |
| Reference protein length | 409 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

The intended protein is the native reference receptor; codon adaptation concerns the DNA design. These identifiers establish the design source, not sequence confirmation of every laboratory plasmid. Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

### Trace from this CDS to the tested condition

The corresponding [BBa_26LLF3LM module](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26llf3lm) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. Its documentation shows the Or35a-labelled colony plate (photograph 1, lower-right), gel B lanes 1–2, the fixed-cell **Or35a+ORCO** condition and P2 **column 10**. These labels connect the design to the team's preparation records. They do not resolve which saved colony supplied each later assay or independently confirm the DNA sequence.

A user can therefore reuse the CDS design and inspect the module-level observations, while choosing a different transcriptional or reporter arrangement. Such a change should be characterized as a new expression context; neither mCherry brightness nor the fusion's calcium-associated fluorescence measures the abundance or activity of this isolated receptor protein.

### Evidence and limits

This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Those observations must not be counted again as an independent characterisation of this basic part, nor taken as proof of membrane localization or receptor specificity.

Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. The stable-cell study by Zboray et al. provides relevant precedent [2], but the present records do not contain a matched wild-type-versus-adapted comparison. No improvement in expression or sensing can therefore be attributed to codon adaptation here.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,230 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×1; BsaI×1**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

The published CDS includes an ATG start and terminal stop codon. Its promoter, initiation context and polyadenylation must be supplied appropriately for the intended expression system.

### References

1. Sato K, Pellegrino M, Nakagawa T, et al. Insect olfactory receptors are heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels. *Nature* 452, 1002–1006 (2008). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06850
2. Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4



### Additional system-level characterization

Test 2 maps **Or35a+ORCO to column 10**. The corresponding [BBa_26LLF3LM module entry](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26llf3lm#odor-2026-10-21) gives the complete six-addition traces and within the post-addition acquisition changes after subtraction of pre-addition drift. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) define the two time windows, percentage-point units and equal-duration sensitivity calculation.

These measurements belong to the labelled co-expression condition. They do not independently characterize the bare CDS, verify receptor localization or establish a ligand-specific response. The Test 1 paired-round measurements retain their distinct definition and source mapping.

targets.title: Or85b condition: endpoint fluorescence and exploratory Test 1 control contrasts
targets.body_markdown:
### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **1 technical fields** labelled Or85b+ORCO, with **156 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **25/156 (16.0%)**, GREEN-positive **8/156 (5.1%)**, and both-positive **7/156 (4.5%)**. Eligible objects represented 18.9% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

![Or85b+ORCO field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/e6d56c8fe0fceb2b49a6059ed52b4dc1c9933c9d805279643e26cd31707ac238.avif)

*Or85b+ORCO, field 01, fixed-cell image panel. Display windows are BLUE 0–255, GREEN 0–120 and RED 0–180 digital values; brightfield retains exported levels. These display adjustments are not the quantitative input. The analysis uses the original channel TIFFs and the same blank-derived criteria across conditions. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp); the original 100 µm scale bars remain in the channel panels.*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 48/156 (30.8%) | 14/156 (9.0%) |
| p99 | 25/156 (16.0%) | 8/156 (5.1%) |
| p99.5 | 24/156 (15.4%) | 7/156 (4.5%) |

*Counts across all available fields for this condition. p95, p99 and p99.5 are alternative blank-score cutoffs, not confidence levels or independent measurements. The denominator is unchanged across cutoffs.*

Only one field was available, so the denominator of 156 objects describes that field rather than between-field reproducibility. Twenty-four RED-positive and seven GREEN-positive objects remain at p99.5; seven objects are dual-positive at p99. Additional fields and independent cultures are needed before estimating a culture-level fraction.

### Test 1: paired-round fluorescence measurements

**Assay labels.** “Round 1” and “round 2” in the older plot are the buffer and test stages of **Test 1**, not separate tests. Its R/B/D table values are dimensionless (×100 gives percentage points). The later **[Test 2 characterization](#odor-2026-10-21)** below uses the same within the post-addition acquisition minus within the pre-addition acquisition calculation as the wiki, with S in percentage points.

One plate, one well per condition–stimulus combination; raw export headers span **10–11 October 2026**. R = ΔFtest − ΔFblank; B subtracts the same-condition buffer-only well; D additionally subtracts the same-stimulus untransfected-minus-buffer contrast. Full equations, denominators, provenance and exclusions are in [the collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156).

| Well | Addition | ΔFblank | ΔFtest | R | B | D |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A09 | VUAA1 | -0.0179 | +0.0065 | +0.0243 | -0.0357 | -0.0947 |
| D09 | 3-octanol | +0.0045 | +0.0257 | +0.0212 | -0.0388 | -0.1213 |
| E09 | benzaldehyde | +0.0158 | +0.0385 | +0.0227 | -0.0373 | -0.1667 |
| F09 | 2-heptanone | +0.0571 | +0.0508 | -0.0063 | -0.0664 | -0.1629 |
| G09 | valeric acid | -0.0127 | +0.2040 | +0.2167 | +0.1567 | +0.1121 |
| H09 | buffer only | -0.0602 | -0.0002 | +0.0600 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 |

B and D for the buffer row are zero by construction. Rows B (ethyl propionate) and C (isopentyl acetate) are excluded from retained comparisons because of reported gain changes; their raw data remain in the archive. Nominal VUAA1 final concentration is 50 µM in the source report, not independently verified. Final VOC molarity, numeric detector gain and matched DMSO vehicle concentration remain unresolved.

![Or85b: two sequential measurement rounds](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/75f8d139eae38b346860f7b1c57a1e604a1dea08d878ec624e8475bb5aacff05.avif)

*Test 1 paired-round plot: plain assay buffer in round 1, test addition in round 2, each normalized to its own baseline. These are two stages of Test 1, not Test 1 versus Test 2. Plain buffer is not a documented DMSO-matched vehicle. The plot shows both individual rounds; the table supplies R and the between-well B and D contrasts.*

targets.title: The Drosophila olfactory co-receptor coding sequence
targets.body_markdown:
The published sequence is **1,461 bp**, including an ATG start and terminal stop codon, for a 486-amino-acid reference protein. Team design records identify *Drosophila melanogaster* Orco (historically Or83b), FlyBase **FBgn0037324 / FBtr0078794**, RefSeq **NP_524235**, with human codon adaptation and synthesis by GenScript.

### Biological rationale and use

Orco participates with tuning receptors in insect heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. Work in Drosophila also establishes a role in receptor localization and function [2]. These findings motivate co-expression with a tuning receptor, but they do not prove that our particular construct reaches the HEK293 plasma membrane.

VUAA1 can activate Orco-containing channels, including Orco without a tuning receptor, in published systems [3]. In this collection it is used as a functional probe, with the qualification that fluorescence changes require controls before being assigned to channel activation.

Use this bare CDS to choose your own reporter or expression arrangement. The provided composite `BBa_26E11Z80` joins GCaMP6f to the Orco N-terminus through a 15-amino-acid linker. Removing or relocating domains creates a different construct and requires a new characterization.

### Functional architecture

![DmOrco coding sequence within the shared sensing system](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/ab4b045e4a28727466318d8c3e9c61df71067e6b1e0c2183c89619b62c9adbd4.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. This basic CDS supplies the shared co-receptor sequence. In BBa_26E11Z80 its N-terminus is joined to the reporter through the linker; the ORCO-only assay label refers to that complete fusion, not this isolated CDS.*

### Which observations belong to this component

The ORCO-labelled construction plate and paired gel A lanes 1–2 are preserved on the [fusion page](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80). They establish the presence of an ORCO-labelled preparation in the workflow, but the labels do not resolve whether a standalone Orco plasmid or the fusion was photographed. They are not reassigned as sequence confirmation of this basic part.

The later fusion-only condition is useful as a control for the ten tuning-receptor modules. Its retained D values include +0.1725 for VUAA1, +0.1056 for 2-heptanone and +0.1298 for valeric acid. Thus, positive fluorescence contrasts in the collection cannot automatically be attributed to the tuning receptor. The complete fusion and its cellular background must be considered. Reusing the bare Orco CDS without GCaMP6f requires a separate readout and a fresh characterization of that arrangement.

### Characterisation status

This untagged CDS was not tested separately. The P2 column labelled “ORCO only” contains the **GCaMP6f–Orco fusion without a tuning receptor**, not this naked CDS. Its microscopy and VUAA1-associated measurements belong to the composite. They cannot be reassigned as independent functional evidence for this basic part.

Reference-protein identity is a design intention. Colony growth and undigested plasmid gels do not replace sequence confirmation of the experimental clone, and the published sequence's assembly sites should be checked before use.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,461 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×2; BsaI×1**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### References

1. Sato K, Pellegrino M, Nakagawa T, et al. Insect olfactory receptors are heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels. *Nature* 452, 1002–1006 (2008). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06850
2. Benton R, Sachse S, Michnick SW, Vosshall LB. Atypical membrane topology and heteromeric function of Drosophila odorant receptors in vivo. *PLoS Biology* 4(2), e20 (2006). https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.0040020
3. Jones PL, Pask GM, Rinker DC, Zwiebel LJ. Functional agonism of insect odorant receptor ion channels. *PNAS* 108, 8821–8825 (2011). https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1102425108



### Additional parent-system characterization

The [parent reporter–Orco fusion](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80#odor-2026-10-21) includes the complete Test 2 ORCO-only profile, using within the post-addition acquisition change minus within the pre-addition acquisition drift. Its [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) distinguish this calculation from Test 1 and retain the equal-duration sensitivity result. The ORCO-only label refers to the assembled fusion-system condition; it does not establish an independent measurement of untagged Orco or compare alternative component designs.

targets.title: A calcium-dependent fluorescent domain for a translational fusion
targets.body_markdown:
GCaMP6f is a genetically encoded calcium indicator described by Chen et al. [1]. Calcium-dependent changes in the calmodulin–peptide/circularly permuted GFP architecture alter green fluorescence. The team design attributes the source to Addgene plasmid #40755 [2].

The published part sequence is **1,245 bp**. It starts with `GTG`, not an initiator `ATG`, and does not end with a stop codon; this submitted fragment is intended for an in-frame fusion context. In `BBa_26E11Z80`, an upstream RSET leader supplies the translation start and the downstream linker connects it to Orco. A standalone expression design needs a suitable start context, reading frame and termination sequence.

### Why this domain

The fast GCaMP6 variant offers a literature-supported starting point for following changing calcium signals. Its performance in neuronal studies does not specify the kinetics, sensitivity or dynamic range of this Orco fusion in HEK293 cells. Our manual-addition, 12-second sampling assay cannot independently resolve channel-opening kinetics or show that indicator speed is limiting.

GCaMP fluorescence is an intensity measurement. It can change with reporter abundance, cell number, optical conditions and the cellular environment as well as calcium. Therefore, changes in signal are not automatically receptor responses. Gain should be fixed and the measurement range checked experimentally; no universal baseline percentage or saturation margin is established here.

### Functional architecture

![GCaMP6f domain within the reporter fusion](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/8ae92945f7e933b3c28f38efc407b7175d9cfe18bcd7cd80697b3a33b37566a5.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted 1,245 bp domain begins with GTG and has no terminal stop codon. The parent fusion supplies its translation start upstream and continues through the linker into Orco; this is not a standalone complete expression cassette.*

The parent [BBa_26E11Z80](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80) supplies the relevant fixed-cell and kinetic observations. In its fusion-only image condition, 24/342 eligible objects were GREEN-positive at the blank-derived p99 cutoff, compared with 1/170 in the blank that also defined the cutoff. The useful distinction for reuse is between having measurable green fluorescence and having a calibrated calcium indicator in a new context. The first is supported by the parent condition. The second would require an independent calibration of the chosen expression arrangement; these data do not determine a calcium concentration, affinity or dynamic range.

The free indicator was not measured independently. Endpoint microscopy and P2 measurements were made on constructs containing the domain and are reported on the parent fusion page. targets.title: Or67a coding sequence for assembly into an olfactory receptor expression system
targets.body_markdown:
### Intended role and assembly

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This CDS supplies the Or67a subunit. For this platform it is co-expressed with the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`; a response depends on the assembled system and the cellular context. The isolated sequence is not a complete sensing device.

Use this part to choose your own promoter, expression marker or fusion arrangement. The corresponding bicistronic module includes a GCCACC initiation context and IRES-mCherry. For either design, supply suitable transcriptional control and polyadenylation from the mammalian vector, and verify start/stop codons and reading frame against the actual assembled sequence. Expression, localization and channel function require separate checks.

### Functional architecture

![Or67a CDS in the expression-module context](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/bf02f2c89732a0edf008fc913da29edd1eb2cfbc5eee0cc7621c973b2066ed65.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted Or67a CDS is the basic part; GCCACC initiation context, EMCV IRES and mCherry belong to the assembled expression module, not this isolated sequence. The calcium-reporter/Orco construct is a separate partner. The diagram does not assert experimental localization or activity.*

### Sequence provenance

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0036009](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0036009.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0076375 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_524005](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_524005) |
| Reference protein length | 407 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

The intended protein is the native reference receptor; codon adaptation concerns the DNA design. These identifiers establish the design source, not sequence confirmation of every laboratory plasmid. Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

### Trace from this CDS to the tested condition

The corresponding [BBa_265G8CE1 module](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-265g8ce1) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. Its documentation shows the Or67a-labelled colony plate (photograph 2, upper-left), gel D lanes 3–4, the fixed-cell **Or67a+ORCO** condition and P2 **column 06**. These labels connect the design to the team's preparation records. They do not resolve which saved colony supplied each later assay or independently confirm the DNA sequence.

A user can therefore reuse the CDS design and inspect the module-level observations, while choosing a different transcriptional or reporter arrangement. Such a change should be characterized as a new expression context; neither mCherry brightness nor the fusion's calcium-associated fluorescence measures the abundance or activity of this isolated receptor protein.

### Evidence and limits

This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Those observations must not be counted again as an independent characterisation of this basic part, nor taken as proof of membrane localization or receptor specificity.

Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. The stable-cell study by Zboray et al. provides relevant precedent [2], but the present records do not contain a matched wild-type-versus-adapted comparison. No improvement in expression or sensing can therefore be attributed to codon adaptation here.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,224 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×2; BsaI×1**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

The published CDS includes an ATG start and terminal stop codon. Its promoter, initiation context and polyadenylation must be supplied appropriately for the intended expression system.

### References

1. Sato K, Pellegrino M, Nakagawa T, et al. Insect olfactory receptors are heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels. *Nature* 452, 1002–1006 (2008). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06850
2. Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4



### Additional system-level characterization

Test 2 maps **Or67a+ORCO to column 6**. The corresponding [BBa_265G8CE1 module entry](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-265g8ce1#odor-2026-10-21) gives the complete six-addition traces and within the post-addition acquisition changes after subtraction of pre-addition drift. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) define the two time windows, percentage-point units and equal-duration sensitivity calculation.

These measurements belong to the labelled co-expression condition. They do not independently characterize the bare CDS, verify receptor localization or establish a ligand-specific response. The Test 1 paired-round measurements retain their distinct definition and source mapping.

### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **2 technical fields** labelled Or59b+ORCO, with **230 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **38/230 (16.5%)**, GREEN-positive **3/230 (1.3%)**, and both-positive **2/230 (0.9%)**. Eligible objects represented 21.1% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.
